articles.summary: The Magura naval drones used by Ukraine have successfully taken out several key Russian targets at sea, demonstrating their adaptability and effectiveness.
articles.content: Ukraine's naval drones, known as Magura, have successfully taken out several key Russian targets at sea, marking a significant shift in the country's military strategy. The versatility of these drones has allowed them to target not just ships but also helicopters in the air and air defense systems on land, demonstrating their adaptability and effectiveness. This unexpected capability has caught the attention of their manufacturer, who had not anticipated such widespread success. The Magura drone's primary manufacturer, UFORCE, founded by Oleg Rogynskyy, was surprised by its performance, with Rogynskyy himself admitting that he didn't expect these results. "I didn't expect it," Rogynskyy said in an interview, crediting the ingenuity of Ukrainian engineers and soldiers for the drones' success. Ukraine's Magura naval drones have been a game-changer in the conflict against Russia. They've not only taken out S-400 launchers and other high-value targets but also demonstrated their versatility by launching FPV drones that can engage enemy air defenses. The Ukrainian military encourages experimentation with its equipment, allowing soldiers to find new uses for and modify their weaponry as needed. This approach has led to the development of R&D elements near the front lines, where companies work closely with combat units to design systems tailored to specific needs. As a result, manufacturers have been caught off guard by the creative ways soldiers use their products. For instance, one company was surprised when Russian soldiers surrendered to its robot without a fight, while another discovered that Ukrainian soldiers can pack an impressive amount of explosive weight onto its drones. The Ukrainian military's innovative use of Magura drone boats has taken an unexpected turn for manufacturers, who are now seeing their products being used in ways they never anticipated. Ukrainian troops have proposed modifications to robots supplied by Western firms, and companies like ARX Robotics from Germany have been working closely with them to develop and scale these new capabilities. For instance, the Ukrainian military first suggested mounting RPGs on robots, which manufacturers then helped to implement. The Magura drone boats have proven themselves to be versatile assets in Ukraine's naval warfare efforts, capable of launching missiles and drones, deploying uncrewed ground vehicles for amphibious assaults, and even engaging Russian naval drones in maritime gun battles. The recent conflict in Ukraine has accelerated the development of naval drone technology, with military officials now acknowledging that crewed fleets may not be sufficient on their own to meet modern maritime challenges. Military leaders are increasingly recognizing the value of combining traditional warships with unmanned assets like drones and other naval vessels to create a hybrid fleet. articles.title: Male Enhancement Procedures on the Rise in US
articles.summary: A new documentary sheds light on a growing trend in male enhancement procedures, with many men seeking penis filler injections as a solution to perceived problems.
articles.content: A new documentary has shed light on a growing trend in male enhancement procedures. According to the film Manhood, many men are seeking out penis filler injections as a solution to perceived problems with their penises. The subjects of the film often express feelings of shame and regret about their bodies. The documentary follows several patients who have undergone the PhalloFILL procedure at a Dallas-based medspa operated by Bill Moore. These individuals include Ruben, an aspiring comedian, and David, a former OnlyFans star whose previous filler procedure had gone awry. The film's director, Daniel Lombroso, spent years building trust with his subjects before they agreed to share their experiences on camera. The patients in the documentary attribute their decision to undergo penis enlargement procedures to a range of motivations. Some see it as a way to escape middle-aged ennui or a difficult past, while others view it as a means to save their marriages. The procedure is marketed as a non-surgical solution that can add meaningful girth to the penis. The cost of the PhalloFILL procedure is significant, with patients paying upwards of $6,000 for each injection session. This has contributed to the growth of a nationwide industry focused on male enhancement procedures. According to Lombroso, the industry's popularity is not limited to men seeking to improve their physical appearance. Lombroso spoke about his experiences filming Manhood at SXSW. He revealed that he had spent years building trust with Moore and his patients before they agreed to share their stories on camera. The film's premiere was a success, and it will be available to stream in November. GQ sat down with Lombroso after the premiere of Manhood. They asked him about his own reactions to the footage he captured during filming. Lombroso admitted that he is generally squeamish but found that being behind the camera gave him a sense of detachment from the subject matter. The film's portrayal of penis enlargement procedures has been described as unflinching and graphic. However, Lombroso argued that it is not the most disturbing aspect of the documentary. He pointed out that one of the patients, Ruben, struggles with his stand-up comedy career in a way that is more unsettling than the physical appearance of the patients. The popularity of penis enlargement procedures has led to significant profits for those involved in the industry. According to Lombroso, some individuals are already reaping financial rewards from their involvement in this growing market. The process of documenting such intimate procedures can be grueling for even seasoned professionals. This project required a delicate balance between capturing the raw emotion and sparing audiences from the most graphic details. A cinematographer's expertise was invaluable in this endeavor, allowing the team to navigate the complexities of the subject matter with sensitivity. The collaboration with Vittoria Campaner brought a unique perspective to the project. One of the most challenging aspects of filming these procedures was witnessing the aftermath of botched surgeries. In one instance, a patient had undergone a penile reconstruction that left him severely disfigured. The decision to omit some of the more graphic footage was not taken lightly, but it allowed the team to maintain a level of respect for their subjects' dignity. By choosing what to show and what to conceal, they aimed to strike a balance between education and tact. Having worked on similar projects in the past, including a documentary about the Brazilian butt lift, provided some insight into the emotional toll these procedures can take on those involved. The experience was not unlike filming in a newsroom, where one must remain detached from the subject matter. Despite the challenges, making this film allowed for a level of separation that helped the team navigate the difficulties of their work. This sense of detachment is crucial when dealing with sensitive topics like cosmetic surgery gone wrong. The reaction to the documentary has been telling, with some viewers expressing shock at the graphic nature of the procedures. However, others have praised the film's ability to tackle a difficult subject with sensitivity and candor. The divide in reactions highlights the varying levels of comfort people have when confronted with images of the human body, particularly those that are considered taboo or unconventional. This disparity is evident in the way different demographics respond to such content. The transition from serious documentaries to a more lighthearted topic like penis enlargement may seem unusual, but it was a deliberate choice made by the filmmaker. Their previous projects had tackled heavy subjects such as the alt-right and personal experiences in the Holocaust. The change of direction was prompted by a desire to explore a cultural phenomenon that is often difficult to address. The filmmaker's business partner joked that this documentary would be the first time they didn't have a connection to the Holocaust, highlighting the shift in focus. Research for the film began three and a half years ago, when stories about the male loneliness epidemic were dominating headlines. However, it was another trend that caught the filmmaker's attention - the rise of penile enhancement procedures. The explosion in demand for these treatments sparked curiosity, but it wasn't the enlargement itself that interested the filmmaker as much as using it as a lens to examine the broader cultural conversation surrounding body image and masculinity. To gain insight into this phenomenon, the filmmaker spoke with urologists who specialize in penile enhancements. They were particularly drawn to the Penuma implant, which has some concerning complications associated with its use. The creator of the Penuma was among those interviewed, as well as practitioners using more permanent dermal fillers for penile girth enhancement. However, many of these experts seemed reluctant to share their experiences openly. The filmmaker's approach to documentary-making involves immersing themselves in the subject matter over an extended period. This allowed them to build trust with their sources and gain a deeper understanding of the issues at hand. Living among patients for two years was a necessary step in making this documentary film. It allowed me to gain their trust and understand the issues they faced on a deeper level. This approach also enabled me to identify potential subjects who were willing to share their stories with me. Finding the right practitioner was crucial, as I needed someone who would be open to my project. After conducting extensive research, I finally came across Bill Moore, an American character whose reputation preceded him. His clinic became a hub for my documentary, where I could observe patients and gain insight into their experiences. Sitting in waiting rooms with camera equipment nearby proved to be an effective way to connect with potential subjects. Some would agree to speak with me, while others politely declined or asked me to return at a later time. This approach allowed me to build trust and establish relationships with the men who eventually appeared in my film. The individuals featured in this documentary are from diverse backgrounds, including a megachurch pastor, a border patrol agent, an OnlyFans star, and someone living with brain cancer. Their stories highlight the various reasons why they chose to undergo penis enlargement procedures. Despite their differing circumstances, all shared a sense of shame and embarrassment about their decision. Convincing these men to share their lives and bodies on camera was no easy task. They were often hesitant at first but eventually opened up as trust was established. This process required patience, empathy, and an understanding that everyone has different comfort levels when it comes to vulnerability. Some participants requested specific boundaries be respected during filming, such as not capturing certain body parts or aspects of their lives. Others gave consent in various forms, allowing me to capture intimate moments within their families. Each individual had unique needs and expectations, which I honored throughout the filmmaking process. The documentary's approach was inspired by direct cinema, where the filmmaker becomes an observer rather than a participant. This style allowed me to immerse myself in the lives of my subjects for at least a year and a half. By doing so, I could capture authentic moments that would add depth to their stories. As I delved deeper into this project, I began to consider the ethics involved in documenting such intimate aspects of people's lives. The recent success of films like [You Can See Everything] has brought attention to these issues and raised questions about consent and vulnerability. The production team behind the documentary made an effort to gain the trust of their subjects, allowing them to share their stories in a way that felt authentic and vulnerable. Ruben, a father of five on his second marriage, was another individual who agreed to participate in the film, despite initial reservations about how his story would be received. The filmmakers' approach paid off with David Smith, an OnlyFans star who had never shared his story publicly before. His pseudonym serves as a reminder that even those in the adult industry may prefer to maintain their anonymity. David's narrative is a powerful and emotional one, touching on themes of shame, vulnerability, and the complexities of growing up evangelical and becoming a male porn star. The production team faced a challenge when it came to featuring David in the film. They had to work with a face replacement company in France, but ultimately decided against using this approach, opting instead to explore other options such as hiring an actor. David's initial reluctance to appear on camera was not surprising, given his background and experiences. However, after being shown the film, he was visibly moved, crying in the room and later opening up to his family about everything. This experience highlights the impact that the documentary can have on its subjects, providing a sense of catharsis and allowing them to confront their past in a way that feels empowering. The fact that David has since become more open and is now touring with the film is a testament to the power of storytelling and the importance of sharing one's experiences with others. articles.summary: The ceremony honored industry legends Glenn Close and Ridley Scott, marking the unofficial start of awards season narratives.
articles.content: The Governor's Awards have kicked off the 2027 Oscars season, marking the beginning of what promises to be an intense and dramatic competition for Best Picture and other coveted awards. Held in a smaller ballroom within the Dolby Theater complex, where next year's main event will take place, the ceremony is a precursor to the main Oscars show. It's here that honorary Academy Awards are presented to industry legends who have yet to receive a competitive Oscar. Last year's marquee honoree was Tom Cruise, while this year's recipients were Glenn Close and Ridley Scott. The Governor's Awards serve as the unofficial starting point for the awards season narratives that will dominate online discourse and watercooler conversations over the next few months. The presence of several films in the room sent a clear message about their campaign intentions. Big-budget productions such as Dune 3, Artificial, and Misty Green made significant impressions at the ceremony. The Governors Awards ceremony marked a significant milestone for several filmmakers and actors as they began their campaigns for Oscars recognition. A24's The Debut, directed by Jesse Eisenberg, made its presence felt at the event, with Eisenberg himself joined by co-stars Paul Giamatti and Julianne Moore in promoting the film. Meanwhile, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim were among those generating considerable buzz, their conversations with attendees a major draw. Their presence was so notable that even Christopher Nolan took time out to chat with them at The Odyssey table. Fielder's meeting with Nolan is an intriguing one, given the two filmmakers' differing styles and approaches, which could lead to some fascinating collaborations in the future. The atmosphere at the Governor's Awards was electric, with an air of excitement that seemed to permeate every conversation. It was as if everyone present knew they were part of something special, a prelude to the main event in March. Despite the buzz surrounding the upcoming Oscars campaign, Fielder remained characteristically nonchalant about his documentary's chances. When asked about his expectations, he opted for a measured response, saying "one day at a time with that signature deadpan delivery that makes it impossible to read his emotions. The Governor's Awards ceremony was indeed an unusual affair, one where the glamour of Hollywood royalty is tempered by a sense of camaraderie and shared experience. It's not uncommon for attendees to mingle freely, as if they're all part of some exclusive club where everyone knows each other's names. As I navigated the room, I found myself starstruck by the sheer number of A-listers in attendance. From Olivia Wilde and Seth Rogen to Penelope Cruz and Ed Norton, it seemed like every notable face in town was there, rubbing shoulders with lesser-known talents like Daniel Kaluuya. As I navigated the Governors Awards room with a glass of Johnnie Walker in hand, an executive approached me with a mixture of amusement and surprise, asking incredulously if I had just been carded by the bartender. The bartender's response was that he thought I looked like, 14 - a humorous observation that left the two of us chuckling. Nearby, David Corenswet seemed oblivious to the commotion, his expression unwavering as ever. When I mentioned James Gunn's recent departure from DC, Corenswet laughed and replied with a genuine shrug, above my pay-grade." His nonchalance was a welcome respite from the evening's buzz. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II caught up with me later, beaming with excitement about his upcoming red carpet appearance for the Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premiere. He revealed that this film marked a unique experience - he had only read his scenes for the project, leaving him to discover the rest of the story like a fan. The ceremony's emotional highs were palpable, particularly during the tributes to industry legends. John Malkovich delivered a heartfelt toast to Glenn Close, expressing admiration for her remarkable body of work. Matt Damon brought the house down with an impressive impression of Ridley Scott from their time on The Martian. His comedic timing and mimicry skill left the audience in stitches. The evening's speeches were also noteworthy, with many speakers conveying gratitude and humility. Notably, Matt Damon made a poignant comment about it being time for Ridley Scott to receive an Oscar, which sparked a standing ovation. In her remarks, Glenn Close addressed her eight nominations without a win, but emphasized that the true reward lies in the work itself. Her daughter's emotional reaction to her speech added poignancy to the moment. The Governors Awards ceremony was marked by moments of levity, as Todd Haynes presented an award to Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler in a humorous anecdote about their shared past. Haynes' lighthearted revelation served as a contrast to the growing narrative that this year's Oscars campaign is long overdue for certain industry stalwarts. articles.title: Environmental Benefits Linked to Employment Nondiscrimination Acts
articles.summary: A new study has uncovered significant environmental benefits associated with employment nondiscrimination acts (ENDAs), revealing a previously unknown link between fairer workplaces and reduced manufacturing waste.
articles.content: A new study has uncovered significant environmental benefits associated with employment nondiscrimination acts (ENDAs), revealing a previously unknown link between fairer workplaces and reduced manufacturing waste. Researchers at Penn State University have been examining 33 years of data on over 8,000 facilities across the US, and their findings suggest that ENDAs are linked to a nearly 10% reduction in manufacturing process waste at firms reporting to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in states with such policies. The study's authors attribute this connection to two key factors: an increase in diverse perspectives within workplaces and a heightened sense of "psychological safety among employees. This safety net, they argue, enables workers to speak up when they identify issues or opportunities for improvement. A greater diversity of voices and viewpoints can lead to more effective problem-solving and innovation, while the increased willingness to share concerns also contributes to improved workplace efficiency. This synergy between fairer workplaces and environmental sustainability is a significant discovery that challenges traditional assumptions about the relationship between social policies and economic outcomes. ENDAs have been widely adopted in recent years as a means of promoting fairness and inclusion within workplaces, but their impact on manufacturing waste has only now come under scrutiny through this Penn State-led research project. The presence of diverse employees in a workplace has been shown to lead to improved operations and reduced waste in manufacturing settings. Firms that implemented Employment Nondiscrimination Acts (ENDAs) saw significant increases in the likelihood of modifying their production processes, with odds rising by 57% compared to those that did not enact such policies. Internal knowledge played a more prominent role in these firms' decision-making processes, with companies relying on it 74% more often when making changes to their manufacturing procedures. This shift in reliance away from external sources may contribute to reduced waste and improved efficiency. The increased diversity and sense of psychological safety that resulted from ENDA enactment allowed employees to feel more comfortable sharing unconventional ideas or questioning established practices, ultimately leading to a more dynamic and adaptive production environment. The researchers used data from the Environmental Protection Agency's Toxics Release Inventory to analyze how ENDAs affected manufacturing waste. This inventory tracks the release of various chemicals and the measures facilities take to reduce pollution on site, making it a valuable resource for studying environmental performance in the context of operations quality. A total of 8,670 distinct manufacturing facilities under 1,112 parent firms were examined between 1987 and 2019. The researchers compared changes in states that had enacted ENDAs to those that had not yet adopted these policies. The absence of federal protections for employment based on sexual orientation or gender identity until the 2020 Bostock v. Clayton decision highlighted a significant gap in existing laws, prompting many states to enact ENDAs and codify expanded protections. The researchers utilized a natural experiment setup, leveraging the staggered adoption of ENDA policies across different states to isolate their effects on manufacturing processes. This approach allowed them to control for other economic shifts that might have influenced production. The study drew on data from the Correlates of State Policy Project, which compiles state-level policy and socioeconomic information over a century. To ensure accuracy in their findings, co-author Max Ji emphasized the importance of robustness checks. We conducted a battery of robustness checks," he said, to verify that there were no pre-existing trends before the policy change, no anticipation of the policies, and that we accurately captured the timing of the impacts. These checks helped to rule out potential biases in their analysis. The researchers performed two distinct analyses: one at the facility level, examining individual manufacturing plants within states with ENDA adoption; another at the firm level, focusing on broader parent companies whose headquarters were located in those states. This dual approach allowed them to assess the policy's impact across different levels of production. While labor and production occur primarily at the facility level, the study surprisingly found that ENDA enactment had a more significant effect at the firm level. According to Muthulingam, this outcome highlights the influence that top management can exert throughout an organization. Firms overseeing multiple facilities in various states may be able to apply broader changes, while increased diversity within managerial ranks and beyond plays a crucial role. The researchers noted that firms with headquarters in states adopting ENDA policies experienced significant reductions in manufacturing waste. These findings underscore the importance of considering organizational dynamics when assessing policy impacts on production processes. By examining both facility- and firm-level effects, the study provides valuable insights into how workplace policies can influence environmental outcomes. A diverse range of perspectives can be instrumental in identifying workplace inefficiencies and finding solutions to improve processes. The study's findings align with emerging research trends in operations management that prioritize employee welfare and societal impact alongside traditional measures of success. Firms that prioritize employee well-being and create inclusive work environments are likely to see benefits for their operations, according to one researcher. The end result is not just about efficiency, but also about creating a workplace where employees feel valued and included, he noted. A study on employment nondiscrimination acts has revealed a surprising side effect: significant reductions in manufacturing waste. The research suggests that when workplaces prioritize fairness and equality, it not only benefits employees but also leads to more efficient operations. The findings indicate that companies with fairer work environments tend to produce less waste, likely due to the increased morale and motivation of their staff. This, in turn, has a positive impact on the environment and contributes to a company's overall sustainability efforts. articles.title: Tulåh Clinical Wellness Opens in Kerala Combining Ayurveda and Modern Medicine
articles.summary: The wellness retreat in Kerala, India blends ancient traditions with modern medicine to offer a unique approach to longevity-focused care.
articles.content: A new wellness retreat has opened in Kerala, India, blending ancient traditions with modern medicine in a unique approach to longevity-focused care. The country's rich spiritual heritage is evident in its numerous wellness centers, scattered across the Himalayas, Goa's beaches, and Varanasi's sacred riverbanks. As an author who explores ancient health traditions worldwide, I've had the privilege of visiting many such centers over the past decade. My husband, a Delhiite by birth, often joins me on these trips to India, where we live in New York but visit regularly to stay with family and explore the country together. That's why I was intrigued when I heard about Tulåh Clinical Wellness, which opened earlier this year in Kerala and combines traditional Ayurveda with modern diagnostic testing. While some Indian wellness retreats have already incorporated a mix of global healing traditions, Tulåh's blend is more akin to a clinical European med spa, but one rooted in ancient medicine. Its location in Kerala was particularly notable, given the state's history as the epicenter of Ayurveda in India. The 30-acre property of Tulåh is situated amidst a rewilded forest and medicinal gardens within the Western Ghats mountain range. The lush surroundings are characterized by an abundance of healing herbs and plants that infuse the air with a distinct earthy scent. As I began my stay, I was greeted with a refreshing watermelon elixir welcome drink and given a tour of the property. This international wellness campus-like setting is enhanced by its Indian heritage, making it feel even more global than expected. The sanctuary's design draws inspiration from Auroville, an experimental community in Tamil Nadu that brings people together to live in harmony across cultures. Tulåh, which means "balance" in Sanskrit, embodies a similar world-blending vibe. The property's 65 suites were designed by Lami Architects and are built on the site of a former cotton mill. From the outside, the sleek, flowing curves give a nod to the legendary Zaha Hadid's style. Inside the nine main buildings, minimalist interiors focus on Indian craftsmanship, featuring terrazzo floors sourced from artisans in Rajasthan, handwoven earth-toned rugs, and marble from Uttar Pradesh. Plush furniture designed by a studio in Kerala adds a touch of local elegance. As I explored the property, the soundscape shifted seamlessly between French electro-pop duo Poom's music and a bamboo flutist performing peaceful South Indian Carnatic meditations in the lobby. This deliberate mix of influences is thoughtfully curated to create an immersive experience. The brain behind this unique blend of traditions is founder Faizal Kottikollon, an entrepreneur and philanthropist born in Kerala who later settled in Dubai. He drew from his upbringing in Ayurveda and his engineering background to craft a holistic wellness retreat that blends the best of both worlds. Kottikollon's wellness retreat, Tulåh, has been making waves since its February opening, and it seems his holistic approach is paying off. The 21-day panchakarma treatment and mamsa kizhi massages with warm cloth bundles of goat meat, milk, rice, and herbs are just a few examples of the traditional Ayurvedic practices being used at Tulåh. These treatments have been shown to be highly effective in strengthening muscle tissues, as evidenced by Kottikollon's own experience. He underwent the treatment after suffering from compression issues, and his subsequent MRI scans revealed that he had made significant progress towards recovery. In fact, today Kottikollon claims to be 99% recovered from his condition, a testament to the effectiveness of Ayurvedic medicine in conjunction with modern medical practices. When asked about his experience, Kottikollon emphasized the importance of integrating traditional and modern medicine rather than pitting them against each other as separate entities. He believes that this integration is key to unlocking the full potential of holistic wellness. Kottikollon's vision for Tulåh has come a long way since its inception, with his $100 million investment being put towards creating a truly unique and effective wellness retreat. The wellness program continued with a series of treatments aimed at reducing kapha, a concept rooted in ancient Ayurvedic practices. These sessions were interspersed with more modern medical testing to assess overall health and longevity. Tests included a chest X-ray, a CAC scan, a DXA scan, an MRI - a daunting prospect for those who fear enclosed spaces - as well as dental appointments, psychological assessments, and mobility and fitness consultations. The variety of tests was extensive, but each one contributed to the bigger picture of overall health. The contrast between ancient therapies like shirodhara and modern medical procedures could be jarring at times. However, the underlying goal remained constant: self-knowledge and understanding. This focus on personal growth made even the most intimidating experiences feel worthwhile. The experience had a familiar quality to it - attending classes in school, with each subject represented by a different teacher. In this case, the subjects were aspects of one's own health and wellness, brought together in the MDM meeting. This multidisciplinary team gathering is at the heart of Kottikollon's vision for Tulåh: representatives from nine departments converge to discuss individual results and create customized plans for the duration of their stay. The meeting is a testament to the integration of different approaches to health and wellness. The thought of all these experts discussing one's progress and needs can be unsettling, but in this context, it was clear that every decision was made with the best interests at heart. This emphasis on collaboration and comprehensive care is a hallmark of Tulåh's approach. One key aspect of the MDM meeting is the calculation of an individual's Tulåh Life Index - a proprietary score derived from bloodwork, body composition results, lifestyle factors, and more. The index provides a snapshot of one's overall function, with a target score of 70 or above considered optimal. The wellness retreat in Kerala has taken a holistic approach by incorporating modern medicine into its traditional practices. Fertility doctors advise against strength training during IVF treatments due to the risk of ovarian torsion, which is a valid concern for those undergoing this procedure. A period of IVF can be daunting and intimidating, but it's essential to prioritize one's overall health, especially when trying to conceive. Regaining muscle mass becomes more pressing with age, and in this case, the doctors recommended making it a top priority due to the individual's advancing years. The personalized approach to treatments and meals at the retreat is tailored to each guest's specific needs, taking into account their unique circumstances and requirements. Customized high-protein meals were prepared using locally-grown ingredients, incorporating South Indian fish curries and North Indian specialties like chicken tikka and chana masala. In addition to traditional Ayurvedic treatments, the retreat now offers a range of modern therapies including aquatic fitness and clinical yoga with a focus on alignment. The staff at the retreat is known for their exceptional care and kindness, going above and beyond to ensure each guest feels comfortable and supported throughout their stay. The staff at this wellness retreat goes above and beyond to ensure each guest feels comfortable throughout their stay, including providing a personalized service after treatments. Guests are treated to a post-treatment care package that includes a shampoo and condition on the spot, eliminating the need for them to rinse off medicated oil in the shower. This thoughtful gesture is especially appreciated by those who have struggled with removing Ayurvedic oil from their skin. The retreat's founder hopes this approach will make ancient traditions like Ayurveda more accessible to mainstream audiences. By blending traditional practices with modern medicine, he believes Ayurveda can be adopted more widely and become a more integral part of people's lives. According to the founder, one reason why Ayurveda has not been more widely adopted is because of its association with slippery wooden beds that leave guests covered in oil. He argues that this practical issue has contributed to Ayurveda's relatively low profile. The retreat's unique approach has a lasting impact on guests, who often report making positive changes to their lifestyle after leaving. For one guest, the experience was so transformative that they continued their wellness journey at home, incorporating strength training into their routine as part of a broader commitment to self-care.
